% note: Path, Commit and SHA-256 are each file's entry in the claims ledger's sources field, \{path, commit, sha256\}, so a ledger row and this table cite a file the same way. The commit is the last commit on main that touched the file: for each data file, the commit that added it; for Study~1's reporting definitions, the revision that the Study~1 analysis and the keep-list analyses cite. Each file is read from that commit, and its SHA-256 is checked against the bytes before any table is built.
% note: Item numbers in the appendix tables (`item~N') refer to the numbered items of Study~1's reporting definitions at that revision: the Study~1 analysis cites items 7--24 there, and the keep-list analyses items 1--24.
% note: Code commit: the commit the analysis ran at, from our work log's entry for each driver run (the top-up file stamps its own). Run file recorded: the run file whose SHA-256 the analysis file itself records about its inputs (for the Study~1 analysis, the compact table that $k$ was computed from); each equals the hash in that run's row of our cost records (the run panel). A dash: no such record (our work log names no commit for the curve runs, and the curve files record no run-file hash; the reporting definitions are a text file, not a run's output). Commits here and in the run panel are shortened to their first seven characters.
% note: Tools for the paid runs and the analyses: anthropic==0.125.0, Python 3.9.6, git 2.39.5 (our record of the code used after the locks); the API client pinned in harness/requirements.txt: anthropic==0.125.0.
